  "text": "The envelope had been waiting beneath her door when Mara returned from work, damp at the corners although the afternoon was dry. Her name appeared in the painstaking capitals Eli used to copy from seed packets. The stamp showed a king who had died before either of them was born.

She opened it standing up.

Mara,

Come tomorrow before the orchard loses its light. Bring something to dig with. I put the bell under the apple tree, on the side where we buried the fox.

Don’t stop in the village. They’ll tell you the bridge is gone.

There was no signature, only a small drawing of a ladder. As children, they had added it to messages that were not to be shown to grown-ups.

She slept badly and left before dawn.

At the last petrol station, she bought a garden trowel from a rack beside the windscreen wash. The cashier wrapped its teeth in yesterday’s newspaper. Mara almost asked him about the bridge, then paid and went outside.

The bridge was there. She crossed slowly, listening to the boards settle beneath the tyres.

Beyond it, nettles crowded the lane. She parked where the branches grew too close and continued on foot, carrying the trowel. The orchard wall appeared through the weeds, lower than she remembered.

Mara climbed over where a stone had fallen loose. Wind stirred the apple leaves, showing their pale undersides. She passed the old swing and knelt beside the tree, trying to recall which of its roots had marked the fox’s grave."
